How a cache stores keys and values

Source: vignettes/articles/storage.Rmd
storage.Rmd
library(dazcache)

This article is for when you want to know what a cache’s directory holds: to back it up, to read its files with other tools, or to be sure two calls find the same entry. It assumes you have read Get started.

The directory

A cache is one directory. The database holds every record and index; values too large to keep in it are files under blobs/; tmp/ is where files are written before they are published.

prices/
├── cache.mdbx        every record and index
├── cache.mdbx-lck    the lock that coordinates processes
├── blobs/b7/b795…3745.rds
└── tmp/              files being written, before they are published
A small value lives inside its record in cache.mdbx; a large one becomes a file in blobs/ that the record points at.

Small values and large ones

A value whose encoding is smaller than inline_max (32 KiB unless you choose otherwise when the cache is created) is kept inside the database, next to its record. Anything larger becomes a file. cache_entries() shows which is which:

s <- cache(file.path(tempdir(), "storage"))
cache_set(s, "small", 1:10)
cache_set(s, "large", runif(1e5))
cache_entries(s)[, c("key", "bytes", "inline", "codec")]
#>     key  bytes inline codec
#> 1 large 800031  FALSE   rds
#> 2 small    133   TRUE   rds

The file’s name is the SHA-256 hash of its bytes, so identical values are one file, however many keys hold them. A file is read-only and is never changed in place; it is removed once no key refers to it.

cache_set(s, "large-copy", cache_get(s, "large"))
identical(cache_path(s, "large"), cache_path(s, "large-copy"))
#> [1] TRUE

How a value is encoded

A codec turns a value into bytes and back. By default, a raw vector or a single string is stored as its bytes (codec_raw()), and anything else as RDS (codec_rds()), so a file under blobs/ with the .rds extension is what readRDS() reads. codec_file() stores a file you already have, keeping its extension.

The codec is recorded with each entry, and a read always decodes with the codec that wrote it, whatever the cache’s default is now.

How a key is written

Every key becomes a text, and that text is the key in the database. A string is its own text. Anything else is written in a fixed encoding, the same in every session, R version and locale. cache_key_chr() shows it:

cache_key_chr(list(exchange = "XSWX", date = as.Date("2026-08-29")))
#> [1] "{date=d:2026-08-29,exchange=s:XSWX}"

The encoding is what makes equal values find the same entry:

  • names in a list are sorted, so field order does not matter;
  • a whole number is written the same as an integer or a double, so 1L and 1 agree;
  • a time is its instant, so the same moment in two time zones is one key.
cache_key_chr(list(b = 1L, a = 1)) == cache_key_chr(list(a = 1, b = 1L))
#> [1] TRUE
cache_key_chr(as.POSIXct("2026-08-29 12:00", tz = "UTC")) ==
  cache_key_chr(as.POSIXct("2026-08-29 14:00", tz = "Europe/Zurich"))
#> [1] TRUE

A key whose text is over 512 bytes is stored under the hash of its text instead; you read it by the same value as any other key. An object the encoding does not cover, such as an environment or a function, is refused with a dazcache_key_invalid error rather than being keyed on something that may change.

cache_close(s)
